summary: F1 confirms a phishing-suspect email was delivered to n.guler@aegean.edu from aegean-edu.com.tr (subject: Ekim maaş bordrosu düzeltmesi – IBAN güncelleme), mapped to T1566.002. The Risk Gate escalates at confidence 0.8 based on one access signal with no confirmed abuse chain; VPN appliance KEV claims were rejected as irrelevant to this account.

contrastive.explanation: Rejecting F1 would leave no surviving signal and the policy would land on benign — the opposite of the human-review path we chose.

risk.rationale: F1 is CONFIRMED (0.8): a spearphishing-link email (T1566.002) about a salary payslip/IBAN update was delivered to n.guler@aegean.edu. That is confirmed exposure — a payroll-targeted phishing lure in a university account — but the evidence shows only delivery, not credential compromise, MFA abuse, or any post-intrusion activity, so there is no confirmed account takeover chain to justify contain. The signal is confirmed rather than weak, so monitor understates it; it is not explained away, so benign is wrong. The VPN-appliance KEV claims are explicitly rejected as irrelevant (no sign-in for this account). Because there is exposure with insufficient evidence to confirm takeover, this needs human review (click/proxy logs, credential use, mailbox rules).
escalate_reasons: signals of compromise without a confirmed abuse chain
